HUMAN RESOURCES COMMITTEE MEETING 
MONDAY, NOVEMBER 16, 2026 
NHS NORTH BOARD ROOM 
 
A meeting of the Human Resources Committee was held at NHS North on Monday, November 16, 2026.  Ms. 
Giglio called the meeting to order at 5:30 pm. 
 
Present:  Ms. Giglio and Ms. Lewis 
 
Also Present: Channel 99 Videographer, Mr. Bowse, Dr. Andrade, Dr. Scarpati, Mr. O’Rourke, and Ms. DeGray 
 
 
HR Update 
• Mr. Bowse reported out to the committee: 92 openings, with vacancies across teaching, student support, 
paraeducator, food service, plant operations, and administrative roles. 
• Contractors currently fill the school psychologist and speech-language pathologist positions; the district 
continues seeking direct hires. 
• Three behavior technicians were contracted, with two more expected to start. The discussion also noted 
Constellations’ contracted staff and program support. 
 
Personnel Recommendations 
 
ACTION NAME POSITION SCHOOL DEGREE STEP CERTIFICATION SALARY EFFECTIVE 
Nomination 
Cont. Sub. Fournier, Ann Nurse BR PhD 22 School Nurse $100,386 2026-2027 school year 
Resignation Bowse, Michael HR Director DW         24-Dec-26 
 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the Personnel Recommendations dated 11-16-26.  
Motion passes 2-0. 
 
• Mr. Bowse described current use of 15 contracting agencies and proposed considering an ESS MSP 
model for next school year, potentially through an RFP. 
• Committee members discussed whether contractor costs could be reduced by hiring more staff directly. 
They noted that salary, benefits, retirement, and agency costs need to be compared on a total-
compensation basis. 
• Nine unions and established salary scales constrain flexibility to offer hiring incentives. Participants also 
raised whether contractor placements, particularly paraeducators, align with student IEP service 
requirements and district staffing needs. 
• Recruitment channels include job fairs, education-focused sites, and major employment platforms. 
• Existing efforts include employee surveys, health fairs, and first-year teacher mentoring. Participants 
identified broader onboarding, school-level welcome, job satisfaction, and organizational culture as areas 
needing attention. 
• The future HRIS system was discussed as a way to reduce paperwork and support employee-experience 
work.  
 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to adjourn at 6:04 pm.  Motion passes 2-0.   
 
 
Submitted by Tara C. Kinsella
